derivations.claim: Take the constant functor from the terminal category to Set at the empty set. It preserves every binary product and every equalizer because the relevant source and target cones are all carried to identities on the empty set. This isolates the missing nullary-product hypothesis in the finite-limit criterion.

ex-the-empty-set-is-the-product-of-the-l.scaffold_status: planned-at-step-2; exact authored citations and numbered-step partition must be synchronized at step 5

derivations.claim: Any cone over the discrete class diagram of all sets includes a function from its apex to the empty-set factor, so its apex must be empty. There is exactly one cone with empty apex, consisting of the empty functions to every set, and every cone therefore factors through it uniquely. This shows that some large diagrams have limits even though completeness asserts only small limits.
